semantic_authority.decision_boundary: Adopt the stricter ISN entity-typed zero-overlap trigger only per locus family; a decline retains the shipped trigger and routes known bad rows to semantic repair.

trigger_definitions.shared_mismatch: The parsed trailing locus and expanded DD path share no content token.
trigger_definitions.shipped: Shared mismatch AND locus contains a configured hardware word AND ISN does not type the locus as a place.
trigger_definitions.strict: Shared mismatch AND ISN types the complete locus token as entity.

recommendation.implementation_boundary: If implemented later, add only the adopted locus tokens as codex policy derived against the live ISN locus universe; do not replace the shipped hardware trigger with an all-entity trigger.

signature.canonicalization: Python json.dumps({measurements,families}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True), UTF-8, no trailing newline

families.rationale: All four pairings name a different immediate DD owner: detector, active spatial-resolution zone, optical element, or camera. The owner/geometry authority record already rejects the detector-centre aperture competitor and refuses aperture as a substitute for the missing active-spatial-resolution locus. No pairing in this family corroborates an aperture owner.

The sole path is under grating/summit; live DD parent documentation identifies a grating summit and the leaf as its height. It does not identify a Bragg crystal, so the entity locus is unsupported rather than merely implicit.

The DD spells the same concept structurally through conductor or hardware geometry followed by rectangle or oblique parameters. Literal locus overlap is not expected; a family-wide entity trigger would reject legitimate cross-section coordinates and dimensions.

The sole measured pairing is historical: the Standard Name is superseded. Its DD path is a profiles_2d grid major-radius coordinate, where coordinate-system ownership is structural and need not be repeated lexically. There is no live write-boundary benefit to a family trigger.

The 50 paths use concrete aperture realizations such as pinholes, detector openings, antenna openings, fibre bundles, filter windows, gratings, and polarizers. The generic diagnostic-aperture locus is intentionally not repeated in those DD structures, so zero lexical overlap is not a sound rejection criterion for this family.

This family is mixed. Two equilibrium separatrix outlines are plainly wrong, but ferritic/object/axisymmetric documentation explicitly says the representation is used for each iron-core segment, making height_of_iron_core_segment a supported zero-overlap pairing. A family-wide trigger would therefore destroy a valid attachment; repair the two separatrix rows semantically instead.

The 44 paths name concrete optical-element subclasses or realizations: filters, apertures, fibre bundles, gratings, polarizers, mirrors, crystals, reflectors, and detector windows. The entity superclass is semantically carried by those components even though the literal words optical_element are absent.

The sole schema path says only length measured by a displacement sensor. The IDS documents sensors on various device parts and carries runtime attachment URIs to identify what a sensor is attached to; the DD schema path itself does not assert a passive structure. The current entity locus is therefore an unsupported owner claim at write time.

This family is mixed. Six fragment and mass-centre velocity paths are legitimate pellet-kinematics evidence without the literal pellet token, while two gas-atom paths are suspicious. A family-wide trigger would reject the six supported pairings; adjudicate the two gas rows separately.

The limiter and mobile-unit rows live under the wall IDS; at least the limiter is directly a plasma-facing component. Wall topology supplies the entity class without repeating its Standard Name locus, so the family cannot safely use lexical zero-overlap as a refusal.

Live DD documentation for wall/global_quantities/current_phi explicitly says toroidal current flowing in the vacuum vessel, and the lower gas-injection summary denotes injection into the lower vessel region. Both are supported implicit-owner pairings despite zero literal overlap.

Diagnostic channel wavelength, frequency, and phase paths plus the Thomson laser area/wavelength paths describe the propagating beam even when the DD uses the instrument or laser owner. The seven pairings are normal implicit beam context, not evidence for a device mismatch.
